channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakh Journalist's Widow Details Transnational Repression and Husband's Murder Investigation
item.description: Natalia Sadykova, widow of slain Kazakh journalist Aidos Sadykov, spoke at an OSCE event about ongoing persecution after her husband's murder. She detailed diplomatic espionage, alleged judicial sabotage by Kazakh oligarchs in Ukraine, and digital censorship targeting independent media BACE. Sadykova criticized Kazakhstan's official investigation into her husband's killing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Sells State's 49.07% Stake in UzXCMG Joint Venture for Mining Equipment
item.description: Uzbekistan is selling the state's 49.07% share in the UzXCMG joint venture, located in Urgench, Khorezm region. The company specializes in manufacturing equipment for mining and underground work. The starting price is set at 140.53 billion UZS, with an auction scheduled for October 19.

item.title: Uzbekistan President to Attend CICA Summit in Baku
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Azerbaijan on October 14-15 to participate in the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA). The summit in Baku will focus on strengthening trust, peace, and security in Asia, and institutional development of CICA.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allocates 5.5 Million Hectares of Pastureland to Rural Residents
item.description: Kazakhstan has provided 5.5 million hectares of pastureland to rural residents, significantly reducing pastureland shortages. This initiative, part of a presidential directive, aims to support livestock farming and rural development. The Ministry of Agriculture reported that 13 million hectares have been returned to state control, with 5.5 million designated for public grazing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Annual Heating Tariff Increases Up to 10% from 2028
item.description: Uzbekistan is proposing to increase centralized heating tariffs annually by up to 10%, starting from 2028, adjusted for inflation. The Ministry of Construction and Housing and Communal Services drafted the proposal. Tariffs will be indexed annually from May 1st, with increases not exceeding 10%. The plan also includes separate tariff hikes for heating and hot water from November 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Special Ecological Regime for Greenhouses in Tashkent Region
item.description: Uzbekistan has proposed a special ecological regime for greenhouses in Tashkent and surrounding areas, focusing on 'green' technologies. Allowed heating sources include natural gas, electricity, geothermal, and solar energy. Burning tires, plastic, bitumen, or waste is prohibited. Greenhouses using solid fuel must switch to approved sources by December 1st, with exceptions for those meeting strict technical requirements.

item.title: Customs Regime Boosts Export Potential Through Tax Exemptions
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing measures to expand production and support exports. The 'Processing within the customs territory' regime offers exemptions from VAT, excise tax, and customs duties, aiding businesses. Navoiy region imported over $22.9 million in raw materials for processing in early 2026. Solis Olis LLC utilizes these benefits to produce vegetable oil for domestic and international markets.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces Special Tax Regimes for Self-Employed, Businesses, and Farmers
item.description: Kazakhstan has introduced special tax regimes to optimize taxation for various business types. Self-employed individuals will pay 4% for social purposes. Businesses on a simplified declaration basis will have a 4% rate, adjustable by local authorities. Farmers and peasant farms will pay a 0.5% individual income tax. These measures aim to create favorable conditions for entrepreneurship.

item.title: Zelensky: Air Raid Sirens Silent During Russian Attack on Kyiv; West Did Not Warn
item.description: Air raid sirens did not sound during Russia's ballistic missile attack on Kyiv on October 12. Sirens activated only after initial explosions. Ukrainian President Zelensky stated that Western partners provided no prior intelligence regarding the impending attack. Russia launched five ballistic missiles at the capital.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Energy Ministry Assesses Impact of Russian Gas Pipeline Explosion
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy has commented on an explosion at the Central Asia-Center gas pipeline in Russia's Penza region. The ministry stated that gas supply to Kazakhstan continues normally under existing contracts. Transit of gas to Uzbekistan through Kazakhstan is also proceeding as planned. No deviations in Kazakhstan's gas transportation system have been recorded.

item.title: Taliban Ministry Orders Review of All Residential Township Documentation
item.description: Afghanistan's Taliban Ministry of Urban Development and Housing has mandated that owners of all residential townships nationwide submit their documents, records, and plans for review. This measure aims to ensure urban order, enforce planning regulations, and prevent violations. Owners in Kabul and provinces have one month to comply with the directive.

item.title: Kazakh Hospitals and Polyclinics Received 1.9 Trillion Tenge via Social Health Insurance Fund
item.description: Kazakhstan's hospitals and polyclinics received 1.933 trillion tenge over nine months in 2026 through the Social Health Insurance Fund (FMSM). Finance Minister Madi Takiev reported that funds were transferred from the state budget to FMSM, which then allocated them to medical organizations. An information system, Qalqan, now integrates FMSM and treasury payment processes.

item.title: Uzbekistan Adopts German Experience in Inclusive Education for Children with Special Needs
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing German inclusive education practices for children with special needs. Seminars involving specialists from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and Schwabing Hospital School focused on creating inclusive environments, individualizing education, and reintegrating students. The goal is to develop a national model for hospital pedagogy and foster international research cooperation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Government to Fund Upcoming Maslikhat Elections from Reserve Funds
item.description: Funds for the upcoming maslikhat (local assembly) elections in Kazakhstan will be allocated from the government's reserve funds, as they were not included in the current budget. The Central Election Commission stated that the total cost depends on the number of commissions, campaign duration, and organizational factors. Approximately 75-80% of expenses will cover commission member payments.

item.title: Taliban Fighters Allegedly Steal Valuables from Kabul Home Posing as Justice Ministry Delegation
item.description: Local sources report that armed Taliban fighters, identifying themselves as an inspection delegation from the Ministry of Justice, robbed a house in Kabul's Omid-e Sabz Township. Five fighters allegedly confined residents and stole valuables. Residents complain of increasing lawlessness and mistreatment by the Taliban, with some families reportedly forced to vacate their homes.

item.title: UN Launches Disaster Protection Projects in Baghlan Province Following Devastating Floods
item.description: The UN Development Programme (UNDP) in Afghanistan is implementing flood protection infrastructure in Baghlan Province through the PAIDAAR project. Supported by the Special Trust Fund for Afghanistan, the initiative aims to reduce flood risks and protect homes, agricultural land, and livelihoods, emphasizing community resilience and disaster preparedness.

item.title: IOM Reports 112 Disaster Risk Reduction Projects Implemented Across Afghanistan Since 2025
item.description: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has implemented 112 projects across Afghanistan to reduce natural disaster risks since 2025. The organization emphasized that preparedness and early action strengthen resilience in vulnerable areas, while also enhancing local capacities in coordination and technical skills for disaster risk reduction.

item.title: Kazakhstan Mandates Increased Share of Domestic Products in Retail Stores Starting October 20
item.description: Starting October 20, Kazakhstan will require retail chains to ensure a mandatory share of domestic products across all product categories. The Minister of Trade and Integration announced that 72 memorandums have been signed to promote Kazakhstani products. Retail trade volume increased by 16% year-on-year, reaching 20.5 trillion tenge in the first nine months.

item.title: Kazakhstan Police Block Thousands of Fraudulent Websites and Advertisements
item.description: In the Atyrau region of Kazakhstan, approximately 3,000 phishing websites and fake advertisements were blocked using the 'Cybercontrol' program. Over 21.2 million tenge belonging to victims was also recovered through the 'Antifraud Center' system. Authorities registered 484 fraud cases this year, with 126 solved and 38 individuals identified.

item.title: Former Boyfriend Sentenced to 14 Years for Stabbing Death of 20-Year-Old Woman in Abai Region
item.description: A court in Semey has sentenced a young man to 14 years in prison for the brutal stabbing death of 20-year-old Dilnaz Zhumagulova in the Abai region. Her body was found with 14 stab wounds. The court also ordered the defendant to pay 20 million tenge in moral damages and over 1.1 million tenge in material losses.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Expand International Research in Pediatric Oncology
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to enhance international research and collaboration in pediatric oncology as part of its National Plan for 2025-2035. The country plans to partner with organizations like the WHO and St. Jude Children's Research Hospital to adopt modern diagnostic and treatment methods. At least 200 specialists will be trained by 2030.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces New Financing Mechanisms to Strengthen Support for Entrepreneurs
item.description: Kazakhstan has implemented new financing mechanisms, including the 'Orleu' program and a special guarantee fund with second-tier banks, to boost entrepreneurship. Mobile support centers are also operating in regions. The government aims to create conditions for domestic production to be more profitable, according to Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Increase Heating and Hot Water Tariffs, Tashkent by 30%
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to raise heating and hot water tariffs for the population starting November 1, 2026, as per a draft government resolution. In Tashkent, tariffs for heating, hot water, and heat energy are proposed to increase by 30%. These changes aim to gradually align tariffs with service costs by 2030.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Own Car Brand Remains Under Discussion, Negotiations Ongoing
item.description: Kazakhstan is still exploring the possibility of creating its own automotive brand and is in talks with foreign manufacturers. The vice-minister of industry stated that the initiative requires careful evaluation due to existing competition, and specific launch details are premature.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister Discusses Bilateral Ties and International Relations with Qatar's Ambassador
item.description: Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi met with Qatar's ambassador to Afghanistan, Mardef Al-Qashouti, in Kabul. They discussed bilateral relations and Qatar's role in facilitating the Taliban's international engagement. Muttaqi noted expanding global ties, while the ambassador affirmed Qatar's commitment to strengthening these relationships.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Economy Minister Details Public Sector Salary Increases
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of National Economy, Serik Zhumangarin, outlined plans for public sector salary hikes. A new remuneration system effective January 1, 2024, increased average salaries by 1.9 times, with lower-paid employees seeing a 2.2 times rise. Further increases of 16% are planned for low-paid workers in 2025.

item.title: Kazakhstan Pensioners Withdraw 490 Billion Tenge Early From Unified Pension Fund
item.description: Early withdrawals of pension savings in Kazakhstan have reached 490 billion tenge since the start of the year, according to the National Bank of Kazakhstan. The majority of these withdrawals, 404 billion tenge, occurred in the first half of the year before minimum thresholds were raised. Pension assets in the Unified Accumulative Pension Fund grew by 6.1% to 26.6 trillion tenge.

item.title: Putin Expresses Concern Over Declining Russian Culture in Central Asia at CIS Summit
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin voiced concerns at the CIS summit in Turkmenistan about the erosion of Russian culture and influence across member states. Despite the organization's history of inactivity, Putin promoted the CIS as a vehicle to maintain cultural and historical ties in Central Asia and the South Caucasus, highlighting a fear of losing cultural dominance.

item.title: Uzbekistan Marks 35 Years of Independence, Emphasizing Human Dignity as Development Basis
item.description: Uzbekistan celebrated its 35th anniversary of independence, with President Shavkat Mirziyoyev outlining strategic priorities for the next decade. The country has undergone significant transformations, prioritizing national values, historical memory, economic opportunities, and human interests. The principle of 'For the sake of human honor and dignity' guides reforms, aiming to protect citizens' rights and improve living conditions.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Economy Minister Explains Discrepancy in Growth Forecasts Between Government and National Bank
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy, Serik Zhumangarin, explained the significant difference between the government's 5.3% economic growth forecast and the National Bank's 3.5% projection. He cited unpredictable external and internal factors, including an accident at Tengiz, issues with the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, and a strengthening national currency, as reasons for the divergence.

item.title: Firearms Used in Altercation in Zharkent, Kazakhstan; Criminal Case Opened
item.description: A criminal case is being investigated following an incident in Zharkent, Kazakhstan, where firearms were used during an altercation between men. Police have initiated cases for hooliganism and attempted murder. One 33-year-old man was hospitalized with gunshot wounds. Authorities have confiscated a weapon and arrested two suspects.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Belgium Leaders Discuss AI's Impact on Higher Education at Forum
item.description: The Rector's Forum, attended by leaders of Kazakh and Belgian higher education institutions, convened at the Alem.ai international center. Discussions focused on the impact of artificial intelligence on education and scientific research. Participants explored Kazakhstan's role as a regional hub and the integration of AI in academic and educational processes. Several agreements were signed to expand partnerships.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Finance Ministry Assures Tax System Resilience Amid Russian Service Disruptions
item.description: Kazakhstan's Finance Minister Madi Takiev stated that the national tax reporting system operates on the ministry's own servers and databases, with backups in place. He confirmed that taxpayers do not use systems like 1C-Accounting for state settlements. This assurance follows disruptions to Russian services like Yandex Go, which affected some taxi and delivery components operating outside Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Maslikhat Elections May Cost More Than Kurultai Elections, Says CEC Member
item.description: A member of Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission (CEC), Mikhail Bortnik, explained that elections for maslikhats (local representative bodies) could be more expensive than Kurultai elections. This is due to the involvement of 3,022 district election commissions. Funds for these extraordinary elections will be allocated from the government's reserve budget, as they were not initially included in the Republic of Kazakhstan's budget.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Deputy PM Defends Tax Reform Amid Budget Shortfall Concerns
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin stated the tax reform has met expectations, generating 3 trillion tenge in additional budget revenue over nine months. Despite a VAT shortfall, he argued the reform is the economy's sole cash source and performing well, projecting at least 3.6 trillion tenge by year-end.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economic Growth to Outpace China and India by 2026, UN Forecasts
item.description: The UN forecasts that Kyrgyzstan's economy will grow by 8.8% in 2026, surpassing the growth rates of China and India. This projected expansion is expected to position Kyrgyzstan among the fastest-developing economies in the region. The forecast highlights significant economic momentum for the Central Asian nation.

item.title: Body of Former Military Officer Found in Helmand After Five Months
item.description: The body of a former military officer, Allah Dad Badizai, was found in Helmand province after being arrested by Taliban intelligence five months prior. Sources state the Taliban initially denied his arrest but later handed his body over to his family. Human rights violations against former military personnel continue in Afghanistan.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev to Visit Azerbaijan for CICA Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will pay a working visit to Azerbaijan on October 14-15. He will participate in the seventh summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Baku.

item.title: Tajikistan's Fall Conscription Plan Achieves 84% Fulfillment in Ten Days
item.description: In the first ten days of the fall conscription for Tajikistan's Armed Forces, the recruitment plan reached 84% completion. The Ministry of Defense reported on October 12 that over 40 cities and districts had fully met their fall conscription targets ahead of schedule. Previously, the ministry had announced 55% of the plan was fulfilled on the first day.

item.title: Uzbek President to Attend CICA Summit in Baku for Working Visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Azerbaijan on October 14-15 for a working trip. He will participate in the 7th summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Baku. The summit agenda includes strengthening confidence, ensuring peace and security in Asia, and institutional development of CICA. Bilateral meetings with foreign leaders are also planned.
